articles.title: National president Nabin asks BJP State unit not to be complacent while citing T.N. example of Opposition not benefitting from DMK’s failure - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nitin Nabin, BJP national president, warned the Karnataka unit to avoid complacency after the Tamil Nadu elections where the opposition AIADMK did not benefit despite anti-incumbency. He urged them to project themselves as a strong alternative and focus on public awareness against the Congress government's failures.  He also emphasized the need for a pro-people struggle and a comprehensive action plan for upcoming elections, including bypolls and Legislative Council elections. Nabin accused the Congress of using its government as an ATM to fund its national activities.

articles.title: I wasn’t allowed to see her body, mother of murdered girl alleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A grieving mother of a 10-year-old girl who was murdered and sexually assaulted near Coimbatore, alleged that her husband cremated the body without her consent. The woman claims she was given no opportunity to see her daughter's remains and demanded police action against her husband and relatives. Minister for Transport A. Vijay Tamilan Parthiban and Minister for Backward Classes Welfare V. Sampath Kumar visited the girl’s native place in Salem district and provided a relief assistance of ₹7 lakh to the family.

articles.title: Residents block key stretch near Katpadi demanding resumption of water supply - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Melpadi village, near Katpadi in Vellore, blocked Tiruvallala Main Road on Sunday demanding immediate resumption of water supply for household consumption. The villagers, who rely on the Katpadi Panchayat Union for water, have been facing irregular supply due to a malfunctioning motor pump and disconnected pipelines at the newly built Over Head Tank (OHT).  Panchayat officials are working to provide temporary water through private tanker lorries before resuming water supply through the new OHT.

articles.title: Trump says he does not make bad deals, but even Republican hawks doubt that now | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Iran and the US are close to a deal regarding Iran's nuclear program, but disagreements remain. The US has agreed to unfreeze billions of Iranian assets in exchange for restoring pre-war economic conditions, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz. However, both sides have expressed reservations about the concessions involved.  Iran insists on discussing its nuclear program within a 60-day timeframe and rejects language allowing Israel military operations in Lebanon. The future governance of the Strait of Hormuz remains uncertain as Iran and Oman discuss a Persian Gulf strait authority.

articles.title: BJP tried to stitch coalition govt. in Tamil Nadu with DMK and AIADMK on election result day: Congress MP Manickam Tagore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BJP MP B. Manickam Tagore accused DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin of attempting to form a coalition government with the AIADMK to prevent TVK president C. Joseph Vijay from becoming Chief Minister.  He claimed that the DMK's actions were orchestrated by the BJP, and that they will soon strike an understanding with the party, potentially leading to DMK MPs abstaining from voting against the BJP-led government in Parliament.  Girish Chodankar, Congress's in-charge for Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, responded to the accusations by stating that the attacks on the Congress should not be directed at the people of Tamil Nadu who voted.

articles.title: Bridget Phillipson orders review of hidden childcare charges hitting parents | Childcare | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Bridget Phillipson, the education secretary, has asked the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) to review childcare practices, including non-refundable deposits, compulsory add-ons, and restrictions on government-funded places.  This intervention comes amid concerns that parents are still being charged extra for childcare despite the expansion of funded hours under the government's flagship program. The government has announced a "Great Summer Savings" scheme with measures to ease household budgets, but polling suggests many families are struggling to afford additional childcare costs.

articles.title: West Ham go down as Salah and Guardiola make emotional Premier League exits | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tottenham Hotspur secured Premier League survival with a 1-0 win over Everton, while West Ham United were relegated after a 3-0 defeat to Leeds.  Pep Guardiola and Mohamed Salah concluded their long tenures at Manchester City and Liverpool respectively, marking the end of an era in English football.   The final day saw several teams secure European qualification, including Arsenal, Manchester City, Aston Villa, and Brighton.

articles.title: Riz Ahmed says UK spies tried to recruit him on three occasions | Riz Ahmed | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Riz Ahmed, the Oscar-winning actor, has recounted three separate instances of alleged attempts by British intelligence services to recruit him. The incidents involved being questioned at Luton airport, through a family friend, and by a senior BBC executive. Ahmed described these encounters as "slightly ridiculous" and declined all offers.  He also expressed his desire to pursue stand-up comedy in the future.

articles.title: 'AI impact on Indians abroad is highest': How H-1B workers are struggling after Meta, Amazon layoffs - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Indian tech workers in the US are facing significant challenges due to recent mass layoffs at companies like Meta, Amazon, and Oracle.  These layoffs have triggered a 60-day countdown for many, who must secure new jobs before their legal stay expires. The situation has sparked anxiety among Indian communities abroad, as families grapple with job loss, housing, and immigration deadlines. Some workers are attempting to switch to B-2 visitor visas in hopes of staying in the US while searching for employment.  The pressure is mounting alongside widespread layoffs across the tech industry.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Mass layoffs threaten the legal status and livelihoods of Indian tech workers in the US.

articles.title: VIT distributed scholarships worth over ₹100 crore for government school students since 2008: VIT Chancellor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: VIT, under its STARS program, has awarded scholarships worth ₹102 crore to 1,147 students from rural government schools since 2008.  The initiative aims to support high-achieving students who lack financial means for higher education. Chancellor G. Viswanathan highlighted the success of Nordic countries' strong education systems and social welfare models as potential lessons for India.

articles.title: Fatou Bensouda on Israeli threats against her and the ICC | Israel-Palestine conflict | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Fatou Bensouda, former chief prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC), has criticized the threats and pressure she faced while investigating Palestine. She argues that justice is being sacrificed to political interests, citing Israel's attempts to halt investigations and a lack of support from some ICC member states.  Bensouda also addresses US sanctions against the court and questions whether leaders like Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu can be held accountable by the ICC.

articles.title: Gwadar University VC, pro-vice chancellor return home 10 days after they were reported missing - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Babar Yousafzai, an aide at the Balochistan Home Department, confirmed that all four individuals, including Dr Abdul Razzaq Sabir, the vice chancellor of the University of Gwadar, and his staff officer, Irshad Ahmed, along with their driver, Hatim Ali, have been found safe after being missing for 10 days. The group had vanished while traveling from Gwadar to Quetta on May 13th.  Mullah Barkat Baloch, a relative of the pro-vice chancellor, Syed Manzoor Ahmed, confirmed their safe return. Security forces conducted an intelligence-based search operation in the Kardgap area of Mastung.

articles.title: Labour to expand youth work experience and training schemes | Youth unemployment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ministers are expanding youth work experience and training schemes in response to a "quiet crisis" in youth employment. Pat McFadden, the work and pensions secretary, announced plans for 300,000 extra placements over three years, aiming to help nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) find work.  Alan Milburn criticized the government's spending on benefits compared to support for employment, highlighting a generational crisis and increased mental health issues among young people. The expansion of sector-based work academy programs known as Swaps is expected to help reverse this trend.

articles.title: WB government directs districts to set up holding centres for detained illegal foreigners - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal Government has instructed District Magistrates to establish holding centers for detained illegal foreigners and released foreign prisoners awaiting deportation. The directive, issued by the Home and Hill Affairs Department, cites guidelines from the Ministry of Home Affairs.  These centers are to be set up in accordance with MHA guidelines to facilitate the deportation of Bangladeshi/Rohingyas apprehended for staying illegally in the state.

articles.title: ‘Pompeii, but in the middle of a massive city’: the ice age fossil site hidden in Los Angeles | West Coast | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: La Brea Tar Pits and Museum
articles.rephrased_article: The La Brea Tar Pits and Museum, a unique site in Los Angeles that houses over 2 million fossils from the Ice Age, is undergoing a major renovation project. The $240 million project will modernize the museum's interior exhibition spaces, research center, and surrounding park, while preserving beloved features like the Lake Pit.  The Natural History Museums of Los Angeles County, which owns and operates the museum, has partnered with the New York design firm Weiss/Manfredi to create a dynamic and accessible experience for visitors. The project aims to connect the public to the scientific process and raise awareness about the importance of preserving ecosystems.

articles.title: Congress asks its rank and file to be alert against deletion of voters ahead of SIR exercise in Karnataka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders are concerned about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Karnataka, fearing voter suppression similar to what happened in West Bengal. The party has urged its rank and file to remain vigilant and is preparing for potential challenges. Randeep Surjewala, Congress general secretary in charge of Karnataka, emphasized the importance of educating voters about SIR's implications.  The State government is expected to respond to the concerns raised by the party soon.

articles.title: Gunman who opened fire near White House was known to Secret Service | Washington DC | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A gunman, identified as Nasire Best, was shot and killed by federal agents after opening fire outside the White House on Saturday.  The 21-year-old had been known to the US Secret Service for attempting to enter the complex multiple times last summer and was previously involuntarily committed for obstructing vehicle entry. The incident occurred shortly after 6pm, briefly locking down the White House while Donald Trump, who was inside at the time, praised law enforcement's swift action.  The FBI is assisting in the investigation.

articles.title: Republican hawks warn of ‘disastrous mistake’ as Trump nears deal with Iran | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's proposed peace deal with Iran has drawn criticism from Republican hawks, who view it as a concession to Tehran.  Senator Lindsey Graham and others have expressed concern that the deal would allow Iran to maintain its nuclear program and control over the Strait of Hormuz, potentially jeopardizing US interests in the region.  Trump, however, insists that progress is being made and that he has instructed his representatives not to rush into a deal. Mike Pompeo, former Secretary of State under the Trump administration, criticized the proposed agreement as "not remotely America First" and reminiscent of the 2015 nuclear agreement.

articles.title: Choppadandi MLA Medipally Sathyam intervenes to speed up paddy lifting process, mitigate woes of farmers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Medipally Sathyam, MLA of Choppadandi, personally intervened in the paddy lifting process at various procurement centres in Karimnagar district.  Responding to reported vehicle shortages, he persuaded lorry owners to deploy their vehicles for paddy transportation and even boarded a truck to oversee the lifting process at one centre. Local farmers expressed gratitude for Sathyam's efforts in accelerating the paddy collection and alleviating their concerns.

articles.title: 'Heinous crime against humanity': Condemnations pour in after suicide bombing in Quetta - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the suicide bombing in Quetta that killed over 10 people.  The attack targeted a passenger train, leaving several others injured.  China, the UK, Russia, Turkey, Australia, Iran, and other international actors expressed solidarity with Pakistan and condemned the attack as a crime against humanity.  KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also offered condolences to the families of the victims.

articles.title: Iran recounts historic battles in response to Trump’s talk of agreement | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran and the United States have invoked historical battles to portray their conflict as a David-versus-Goliath struggle.  Iranian officials, including Esmaeil Baghaei, drew parallels to ancient Persian victories over the Romans, while Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), emphasized continued resistance against the US and Israel.  Masoud Pezeshkian, Iran's president, linked the current standoff to historical examples of Iranian resilience in defending its territory.  The Iranian government has also highlighted the 1982 recapture of Khorramshahr as a model for future victories. Mohammad Mokhber, an advisor to the Supreme Leader, argued that both former Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein and US President Donald Trump underestimated Iran's power. The latest messaging from Iranian leaders comes in response to Donald Trump’s suggestion of taking control of Iran.

articles.title: Britain’s anxious young adults struggle with modern workplace demands, warns UK govt advisor - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Alan Milburn, a former health secretary, warned that rising anxiety and depression among young people are hindering their ability to adapt to the modern workforce. In his interim report on youth inactivity, Milburn argues that companies need to understand how digital culture has changed younger generations and provide proper mental health support. He suggests flexible working arrangements could benefit both individuals and businesses.  The report highlights a "bedroom generation" of young people who spend excessive time online, impacting their work performance and sleep patterns.  Milburn believes this generation is not lazy or less intelligent but rather anxious and depressed due to their digital upbringing.

articles.title: Regrettable fact that PM Modi has not held a single open press conference: Editors Guild of India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Editors Guild of India (EGI) criticized the recent confrontations between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and foreign journalists during his visit to Norway and the Netherlands. The EGI called for an end to the government's adversarial stance towards the media, noting that Prime Minister Modi has not held a single open press conference since assuming office in 2014.  The organization expressed concern over the stand-offs between Indian officials and journalists, particularly when Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng questioned press freedom and human rights issues in India.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Lack of open press conferences by the PM raises concerns about transparency and accountability.

articles.title: China launches three-crew space flight as part of Moon ambitions - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: China successfully launched its Shenzhou-23 mission, sending a Chinese astronaut to orbit for the first time in a year-long experiment. The Chinese space agency (CMSA) reported that the astronauts are in good condition and the launch was successful.  The mission marks a significant step towards China's goal of landing astronauts on the Moon by 2030, as well as future missions to Mars.

articles.title: Israeli strikes pound Lebanon despite signs US and Iran are close to peace deal | Lebanon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israel continued to strike targets in Lebanon on Sunday despite a ceasefire, resulting in casualties. The strikes targeted multiple locations in southern and eastern Lebanon, including the destruction of a civil defense facility in Nabatieh. Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem expressed hope for an agreement between his group's backer, Iran, and the US that would include Lebanon in its terms.  The strikes come amid anticipation of a peace deal between the US and Iran, which has reportedly demanded the cessation of hostilities in Lebanon.

articles.title: Situationer: Wheat policy failures deepen market crisis - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan national wheat sector is facing a crisis due to structural weaknesses in agricultural planning, procurement management, and food security governance.  Farmers are struggling with low prices and rising input costs, while traders are holding back stocks anticipating future shortages. The situation has escalated into a confrontation between market realities and administrative controls, prompting the Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to order stricter stock declarations. Analysts suggest that the government's attempts to control the market through procurement have exacerbated the crisis by creating uncertainty and hindering market liquidity.  The lack of adequate reserves and inconsistent policies are further contributing to the instability in the wheat sector.

articles.title: Some progress - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's mediation efforts in the Iran-US crisis are entering a crucial phase, with ISPR reporting "encouraging progress" towards a final understanding.  The talks have moved beyond broad appeals for restraint to detailed negotiations on an interim arrangement covering sanctions relief, the Strait of Hormuz, nuclear activities, and guarantees against renewed military action. Iranian officials remain skeptical about US intentions and insist on their national rights, while diplomatic activity has intensified with Qatar joining the mediation effort.  Despite tensions, both sides acknowledge some progress, but major disagreements persist, particularly over Iran's enriched uranium stockpile and demands regarding the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Warrants for defendants skipping court in England and Wales up 50% since 2020 | UK criminal justice | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: English and Welsh criminal justice system
articles.rephrased_article: Channel 4’s Dispatches investigation revealed that almost 60,000 arrest warrants were issued in England and Wales for defendants who skipped court last year, a nearly 50% increase since 2020. The number of outstanding failure-to-appear warrants is over 30,000, meaning thousands of criminals could be on the run after being charged. Alex Chalk KC, former justice secretary, stated that this situation is "a horror show" due to delays in the criminal justice system caused by factors like the Covid pandemic and underfunding.  The investigation also highlighted cases of wanted criminals who have evaded capture despite warrants issued against them.

articles.title: Elusive normalisation - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Dattatreya Hosabale, secretary general of the Hindu extremist organization RSS, and former Indian army chief (retd) Gen Manoj Naravane have called for diplomatic ties with Pakistan, while serving army chief Gen Upendra Dwivedi has stated that Pakistan must choose between being a part of geography or history. The Indian government's stance on normalizing relations with Pakistan is unclear, as it continues to use anti-Pakistan rhetoric and military action against the country under the guise of fighting terrorism.  However, Pakistan successfully defended itself against India's aggression in May 2025, demonstrating that future conflicts will likely be non-contact warfare. The author argues for a more peaceful approach between the two countries, emphasizing the need for bilateral contact and confidence-building measures to prevent further conflict.

articles.title: For third year in a row, Israel blocks Hajj pilgrimage for Gaza Muslims | Civil Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has continued to block the Rafah crossing, preventing Palestinians in Gaza from performing the Hajj pilgrimage for a third consecutive year.  This closure has resulted in the deprivation of over 10,000 citizens and at least 71 pilgrims who had won the official draw. The Palestinian Ministry of Awqaf and Religious Affairs reports that the Israeli blockade has also devastated the enclave's religious tourism economy, leading to the collapse of all 78 licensed travel companies.  The Palestinian Center for Political Studies (PCPS) argues that this intentional targeting constitutes "collective punishment" under international law and violates the rights to freedom of religion and movement. The situation has left thousands of Gaza residents stranded with hopes fading as they await a resolution.

articles.title: Suicide bombing near railway track in Pakistan kills at least 23 people | Pakistan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle near a railway track in Quetta, Pakistan, killing at least 23 people and injuring over 70 others. The attack, claimed by the outlawed Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), targeted a passenger train carrying security personnel.  The incident caused two train cars to overturn and catch fire, damaging nearby buildings and vehicles. Shahid Rind, a Balochistan provincial government spokesperson, condemned the attack, while Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan's prime minister, called it "cowardly terrorism." The Balochistan chief minister, Sarfraz Bugti, vowed to hunt down the militants responsible.

articles.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: REWRITING THE PAKISTAN NARRATIVE - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Imran Khan administration's introduction of the Single National Curriculum (SNC) in 2021 aimed to preserve a state-curated national narrative, but it was ultimately rejected by governments in Sindh and Balochistan. This follows decades of debate over Pakistan's religious identity, fueled by sectarian violence, Islamist terrorism, and political friction between the military and civilian government. Scholars like Aitzaz Ahsan have long advocated for a more nuanced understanding of Pakistan's history, emphasizing its ancient civilisational roots in the Indus Valley. This theory gained traction after the 2010 passage of the 18th Amendment to the Constitution, which granted provinces greater autonomy and allowed them to reintroduce regional histories into textbooks.  The SNC's rejection suggests a shift towards a more pragmatic approach by the state, seeking to address contemporary challenges while integrating aspects of the Indus Theory into its narratives.

articles.title: France bans Ben-Gvir: Which other Israeli leaders have been penalised? | Explainer News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: France has banned Israeli far-right Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir from entering its territory, citing his "unspeakable" behavior towards detained Gaza flotilla activists. Ben-Gvir, who was previously barred by Poland, is among several Israeli leaders and organizations that have been sanctioned or temporarily banned by countries in the West since Israel's war on Gaza began in October 2023.  The European Union has also imposed sanctions on Israeli settlers and pro-settlement groups, while the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant.

articles.title: David Miliband: Europe and US need ‘separate bedrooms’ but not divorce | David Miliband | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Miliband, former Labour foreign secretary, suggested that Europe should maintain a "separate bedrooms" relationship with the US, while still maintaining its alliance. He argued for increased European autonomy in areas like economics, military spending, and AI development to counterbalance the impact of US policies.  He emphasized the importance of economic and environmental interests for Europe's global standing, particularly in addressing climate change.  Philippe Sands and Susan Neiman also discussed the need for a stronger EU-UK relationship, while acknowledging the challenges posed by Brexit.

articles.title: Iran secretly bought Chinese satellite tech via UAE — then struck Abu Dhabi: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Revolutionary Guards of Iran, using a UAE-based procurement network, acquired advanced Chinese satellite communication equipment linked to Tehran's drone and missile program. The shipment, concealed through false navigational data and routed through Dubai's Jebel Ali container port, was delivered to Iran via the Iranian vessel Rama III. This acquisition is particularly sensitive given Abu Dhabi's hardline stance towards Iran and raises concerns about the use of UAE commercial hubs for circumventing sanctions on Iran's military procurement. The US Treasury has sanctioned several entities involved in this transaction, including the Iranian telecommunications company EFK and the shipping agent Blue Calm Marine Services.

articles.title: SC’s revival of Section 124A for consenting accused brings back a colonial law the country did not want - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has revived Section 124A (sedition) proceedings, despite its previous agreement that the provision was outdated and oppressive. The court's May 21 clarification allows for trials under the section to proceed on merits, but this decision does not address the constitutionality of the law itself, which is still being challenged in separate petitions.  The court’s action has created practical challenges, particularly regarding situations where accused individuals may consent to proceedings while co-accused refuse.

articles.title: Neighbour to a superpower - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan and China are celebrating 75 years of diplomatic relations, but the relationship is evolving in a rapidly changing world.  With China's rise as a global superpower, Pakistan faces new strategic dilemmas and dependencies. The partnership has shifted from economic promises to security cooperation, with China increasingly concerned about threats to Chinese nationals and CPEC-related projects. While Pakistan seeks to maintain its balancing act between China and the US, its reliance on China for defense, financial support, and strategic cover deepens.  Despite this deepening relationship, Pakistan continues to pursue alternative avenues for diplomatic flexibility in a multipolar world.

articles.title: Bahrain jails nine defendants for life for ‘cooperating’ with Iran’s IRGC | Espionage News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bahrain has sentenced nine individuals to life in prison for collaborating with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), while two others received three-year sentences. The convictions follow an intensified crackdown by Bahraini authorities on individuals suspected of ties to Tehran and come amidst heightened tensions between Iran and its Gulf neighbors following a wave of Iranian strikes.  The government alleges that some defendants photographed strategic sites in Bahrain on behalf of the IRGC, facilitated financial transfers from Iran, and recruited individuals within the country to support their operations.

articles.title: ‘We’re concerned’: US-based prediction markets taking bets on Australian elections and Albanese’s word choices | Gambling | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: US-based prediction market websites, Kalshi and Polymarket, are experiencing a surge in popularity in Australia despite operating without approval from Australian regulators. These platforms allow users to bet on events ranging from political outcomes to weather predictions, raising concerns among gambling harm advocates who warn of the potential for increased gambling addiction.  While Kalshi and Polymarket claim they have no trading in Australia and are not worried about Australians accessing their sites, experts fear these unregulated platforms could create significant integrity risks and pose a threat to Australian consumers. The Australian Communications and Media Authority (Acma) is monitoring the situation but has yet to take formal action against these websites.

articles.title: At least 14 killed, 20 injured in suicide bombing targeting shuttle train in Quetta: Balochistan govt - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A vehicle-borne suicide bombing targeted a shuttle train in Quetta, Balochistan, killing 14 people and injuring 20 others. The attack, which occurred near Chaman Phatak shortly after 8am local time, derailed three coaches and caused significant damage to nearby buildings.  Shahid Rind, an aide to the Balochistan chief minister, condemned the attack as a "proof of terrorists' confusion" and vowed that the perpetrators would be brought to justice. The Pakistani government has pledged to combat terrorism and ensure the safety of its citizens.

articles.title: ‘A paper city’: New York ‘library’ hosts 3.5 million pages of Epstein files | Human Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A nonprofit called the Institute for Primary Facts has created a physical archive of 3.5 million pages of law enforcement documents related to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein in a Tribeca gallery. The exhibition, titled "The Donald J Trump and Jeffrey Epstein Memorial Reading Room," aims to shed light on the many cases connected to Epstein that never went to trial and provide accountability for victims.  The project was organized with survivors at its center, aiming to generate public pressure for transparency and accountability from the US government.  Visitors have left messages of grief and anger in response to the archive's powerful display, highlighting both a sense of relief and frustration over the lack of justice for victims.

articles.title: Escapes, fires, stabbing: catastrophic security failures revealed in Australia’s immigration detention network | Australian immigration and asylum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Management and Training Corporation (MTC), the private company contracted to run Australia’s immigration detention centres, has been plagued by security failures since taking over operations in 2023. The Home Affairs Minister, Tony Burke, has publicly criticized MTC's performance, demanding immediate improvements.  Multiple escapes, including one involving a child sexual abuse offender who escaped while being escorted to hospital, have occurred under the company's watch. Investigations revealed serious concerns about staffing levels, inadequate safety equipment, and a lack of emergency preparedness at several detention centres. The National Preventive Mechanism, an independent monitor of places of detention, has also flagged "minimalist staffing models" as a major risk factor.  The government is facing criticism for its decision to award the contract to MTC despite previous concerns about the company's track record in the US and Australia.

articles.title: Turkish police storm opposition offices after leaders ousted
articles.rephrased_article: Turkish riot police stormed the headquarters of the Republican People's Party (CHP) in Ankara on Sunday, following a court ruling that declared its leadership null and void. The move further consolidates President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's grip on power.  The party leader, Özgür Özel, vowed to defy the decision and continue fighting for political change. Human Rights Watch criticized the government's actions as undermining Turkish democracy.

articles.title: Ohio State reels from multiple scandals amid wider crisis in higher education | US universities | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ohio State University, a prominent institution in the Midwest, is facing multiple scandals that have tarnished its reputation.  The university has settled with hundreds of victims of sexual abuse by Dr. Richard Strauss, a former medical staff member who abused student athletes for decades.  In addition to the sexual abuse scandal, the university's president resigned after using public funds to support an inappropriate relationship with a podcast host. The university is also grappling with declining enrollment and financial challenges, as well as controversies surrounding diversity initiatives and academic freedom.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Abuse of power and suppression of justice are evident in the cover-up of sexual abuse.

articles.title: Quad remains ‘vital’, says Japanese Foreign Minister, rejecting concerns over the grouping’s importance in the Indo-Pacific - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Toshimitsu Motegi, Japanese Foreign Minister, stated that the Quadrilateral Foreign Ministers' Meeting (FMM) will prioritize cooperation on critical minerals for green energy and hi-tech. The meeting, hosted by S. Jaishankar, will also address ongoing conflicts in Iran and the Hormuz Strait blockade, as well as the recent visit of Donald Trump to China.  The FMM is expected to set the agenda for the Quad Summit, which has not taken place since 2024 due to India-U.S. tensions.

articles.title: In Spectrum: Memory, migration and making of Lahore’s urban soul (Part-I) - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Gawalmandi, a historically significant neighborhood in central Lahore, is more than just a culinary destination. Its origins as a hub for buffalo milk production and trade shaped its identity before becoming a vibrant space reflecting the complexities of urban modernity in South Asia.  The area's transformation after Partition saw migrants from various communities adapt their food traditions to the new environment, creating a unique cultural tapestry. This process involved improvisation, social interaction, and the creation of shared spaces that fostered a sense of belonging. Gawalmandi embodies the concept of "urban conviviality," where everyday encounters contribute to the neighborhood's character. Despite challenges like commercialization and political interventions, its historical significance remains evident in its architecture, food culture, and vibrant public life.

articles.title: UK heatwave expected as temperatures near record highs for May | UK weather | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Met Office has declared a heatwave in parts of the UK, with temperatures reaching near May records. London and surrounding counties have met the criteria for a heatwave, with temperatures exceeding 28C for three consecutive days. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) issued amber heat health alerts for several regions, warning of potential increased deaths due to the extreme heat.  The hot weather is expected to continue into Monday, with highs potentially reaching 34C in some areas.

articles.title: Uefa Champions League Final: UEFA Champions League final: Keir Starmer urges UK broadcaster to air Arsenal vs PSG clash for free - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, the UK Prime Minister, criticized TNT Sports for making next weekend's UEFA Champions League final between Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain a paid event.  He argued that the match should remain free to watch for fans across Britain, emphasizing its importance as a shared sporting moment. TNT Sports defended its subscription model, offering access to all three European club finals through HBO Max for £4.99 per month. The move marks the first time all three finals have been behind a paywall in the UK and ends a long tradition of free-to-air coverage.

articles.title: Nanjangud camp marks Phule bicentenary, calls for protection of govt. schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) organized a one-day children's summer camp in Nanjangud, Karnataka to commemorate the 200th birth anniversary of social reformer Mahatma Jyotiba Phule. The event focused on promoting value-based education and social awareness through interactive sessions and activities.  Speakers emphasized the importance of protecting government schools as envisioned by Phule, who established them to promote education and challenge social inequalities.

articles.title: What we know about the possible US-Iran deal - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced an agreement had been “largely negotiated” with Iran, which would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.  Esmaeil Baqaei, Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, stated that a memorandum of understanding (MoU) would be drafted first, before a final deal is reached within 30 to 60 days. The agreement reportedly includes an apparent commitment by Iran to give up its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, but Iran has denied making any commitments regarding its nuclear program.  A key sticking point in the talks is traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global conduit for oil shipments that has come under Iranian control since the outbreak of the war. The potential agreement would also see the US temporarily lifting sanctions on oil, gas, and petrochemicals during the negotiation period.

articles.title: Blast hits train in Pakistan’s Balochistan, killing at least 24 people | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A bomb attack on a train carrying military personnel in Quetta, Balochistan, Pakistan, killed at least 24 people and injured over 50. The explosion occurred near the Chaman Pattak signal as the train passed, causing two carriages to overturn and catch fire. The Balochistan Liberation Army claimed responsibility for the attack.

articles.title: Andy Burnham seeks advice from Sue Gray on forming future Labour government | Andy Burnham | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andy Burnham has sought advice from Sue Gray, former chief of staff to Keir Starmer, on managing a potential transition into Downing Street.  Senior Labour figures are increasingly treating Burnham's path back to Westminster seriously, with internal succession chatter intensifying ahead of the Makerfield byelection.  Darren Jones, chief secretary to the Treasury, criticized the internal jockeying and urged focus on addressing country-wide challenges. Wes Streeting, a potential rival contender in any future leadership race, campaigned for Burnham over the weekend alongside Lucy Powell, Labour's deputy leader.

articles.title: New U.S. Green Card rules raise concerns among professionals, students - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration's new immigration policy requiring non-immigrant visa holders to apply for permanent residency in their home countries has caused anxiety and uncertainty among Indian professionals and students living in the United States. The policy, implemented through a memo from USCIS, requires most temporary workers and students to leave the country and apply for permanent residency through consular processing, creating concern for those already facing lengthy Green Card backlogs.  Many individuals, including software engineers like Maddela Srinivasulu and parents like Bulusu Janardhan, express fear about the future of their families and careers in the U.S., while others believe the policy's impact will be limited due to existing wait times for employment-based Green Cards.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz lands in Beijing, will hold 'high-level' meetings with Chinese leadership - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in Beijing on Sunday to meet with Chinese leadership, including President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang.  He discussed strengthening the Pakistan-China all-weather strategic cooperative partnership and advancing cooperation under CPEC Phase-II. Shehbaz highlighted areas of importance for Pakistani-Chinese cooperation, such as agriculture, IT, special economic zones (SEZs), and mining. He also emphasized the potential of renewable energy, healthcare, and investment opportunities in Pakistan.  DPM Ishaq Dar, accompanied by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, arrived in Beijing to participate in the 2nd Pakistan–China Political Parties Forum and the 4th CPEC Political Parties Joint Consultation Mechanism. Dar highlighted Pakistan's economic revival and emphasized a billion-dollar joint venture between Servis Group of Pakistan and Long March Tyres of China.  The visit is significant as Pakistan and China commemorate the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations.

articles.title: Trump turnaround: Open the straits, close the war - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump has reportedly shifted his approach to the ongoing conflict with Iran, aiming for a deal that falls short of initial demands. The agreement, which would involve concessions from the U.S., aims to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and prevent global economic disruptions caused by energy supply issues.  However, Iran insists on maintaining sovereignty over the waterway and has rejected commitments regarding uranium enrichment or nuclear program dismantlement.

articles.title: At least 14 killed, 20 injured in suicide bombing targeting train in Quetta: Balochistan govt - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A vehicle-borne suicide bombing on a shuttle train in Quetta, Balochistan killed 14 people and injured 20 others. The attack targeted civilians near Chaman Phatak shortly after 8 am local time, causing damage to nearby buildings and derailed three coaches of the train.  The Pakistani government condemned the attack, vowing to punish the perpetrators. President Asif Ali Zardari called the act a "heinous act" aimed at destabilizing Pakistan. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also expressed condolences for the victims and pledged to eliminate terrorism in all forms. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi visited Quetta and pledged to bring the perpetrators to justice. The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) raised concerns about rising terrorism incidents in Balochistan, highlighting civilian vulnerability.

articles.title: Syria cannot heal without a rebuilt health system | Syria's War | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The European Union and Syrian officials met in Brussels to discuss Syria's reconstruction. The EU has pledged 14 million euros to rehabilitate Ar-Rastan Hospital in Homs, but the gap between the conditions returnees face and their needs for a healthy life remains a major barrier. Relief International reports that many Syrians returning home are unable to access healthcare due to shortages of staff and equipment, long wait times, and lack of medication. The organization also highlights the psychological distress caused by the war and the need for rehabilitation services for those with disabilities.  Rebuilding Syria's health system requires a coordinated effort from the international community, including sustained support and multi-year investments in primary healthcare and mental health services.

articles.title: Russia hits Kyiv with hypersonic ballistic missile in ‘deranged’ attack | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Russia used its hypersonic Oreshnik ballistic missile for a third time in Ukraine, targeting Kyiv and surrounding areas. The attack killed at least four people and injured dozens, according to Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the Ukrainian president.  The strike involved 600 drones and 90 missiles of various kinds, with significant damage reported in Kyiv's districts, including a school fire and a business center shelter incident.  Russia’s defense ministry claimed successful attacks on Ukrainian military targets, while Emmanuel Macron, the French president, condemned the attack as "reckless nuclear brinkmanship." The European Union has pledged to increase pressure on Russia following the attack.

articles.title: Attacks on Ebola centres intensify in eastern DRC amid outbreak fears | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Attacks on Ebola treatment facilities in eastern DRC are escalating, fueled by anger and mistrust over burial protocols. World Health Organization warns the outbreak could worsen.  The incidents include a storming of a health center and a fire at a Doctors Without Borders tent.  Health workers face resistance from communities who fear Ebola is being trafficked. The Congolese government urges safe burials while residents express cultural grief over disrupted rituals.  Authorities are struggling to contain the spread, facing shortages in resources and calls for increased international support.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death case: final rites to be held in Bhopal after second autopsy by AIIMS Delhi team - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Twisha Sharma, a model-turned-actor, will be cremated at Bhopal's Bhadbhada Vishram Ghat on Sunday (May 24, 2026) after a second postmortem examination by a team of doctors from AIIMS-Delhi. The family expressed deep grief and emotional trauma over the delay in performing the cremation, citing traditional Hindu rituals.  Samarth Singh, Sharma's husband, was arrested on Friday (May 22, 2026) for his alleged involvement in her death.

articles.title: SC upholds consecutive life terms in multiple murder cases - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of Pakistan affirmed the Lahore High Court's decision to impose consecutive life sentences on Qaiser Abbas, convicted of murdering two women. The court rejected Abbas' argument that concurrent sentencing was appropriate due to a provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).  Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, writing for the bench, stated that imposing concurrent sentences would diminish the gravity of each murder and create an "artificial equivalence" between taking one life and multiple lives. The court upheld the trial court's decision, finding no grounds to interfere with its findings.

articles.title: Three-day meet to be held in Toronto on Tamils, classical Tamil in the world of AI - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Federation of Global Tamils, Canada, will host a three-day conference in Toronto, Canada in October 2026 focusing on the relevance of classical Tamil in the world of artificial intelligence. The conference will explore themes such as philosophy and culture, economic thought and lifestyle of Tamils, and economic development of North-East Sri Lanka. Abstracts for papers are due by June 10th with full paper submissions due August 31st.

articles.title: “They don’t like each other:” Is Russia and Iran’s alliance falling apart? | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Aleksander Griboyedov, a Russian diplomat, was killed in 1829 after refusing to surrender Armenian fugitives.  Russia and Iran have maintained a complex relationship marked by distrust and pragmatism. The two countries have cooperated on issues like the nuclear program and regional security but remain rivals for influence in the Middle East. Despite their shared interests, Russia and Iran are also competing with each other for resources and strategic alliances. In recent years, Moscow has provided Tehran with military support during the war in Ukraine, while Iran has supplied drones to Russia. The relationship between Russia and Iran is often described as a "marriage of convenience" rather than a formal alliance.

articles.title: Ladakh L-G Saxena launches ecological restoration project to reclaim 800 acres of barren land - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lieutenant-Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena launched an ambitious ecological restoration project in Ladakh, aiming to reclaim nearly 800 acres of barren land near Spituk. The project utilizes excess water from the recently restored Igoo-Phey irrigation canal to replenish depleted aquifers and trigger natural vegetation growth.  Officials believe this initiative will improve soil health, create opportunities for sustainable agriculture and afforestation, and contribute to long-term ecological benefits in the region. This project aligns with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of restoring 26 million hectares of degraded land by 2030.

articles.title: Four CTD men martyred in operation near Quetta - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: CTD personnel and security forces conducted separate operations in Quetta, Pishin, and the Surkhab refugee camp, resulting in the deaths of 13 terrorists and four CTD personnel.  The operations were carried out following intelligence reports about the presence of terrorists. Shahid Rind, an aide to the chief minister on media and political affairs, confirmed the gun battles and stated that security forces will continue their efforts against terrorism. A large quantity of weapons, ammunition, explosives, and other equipment was recovered from the terrorists' hideouts.

articles.title: Gunman shot dead by Secret Service agents near White House: What we know | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A man identified as Nasire Best, a 21-year-old from Maryland with documented mental health conditions, was shot and killed by United States Secret Service officers after opening fire on a security checkpoint near the White House. The incident occurred shortly before 6 p.m. Saturday, prompting a lockdown of the White House. No Secret Service officers were injured, but a bystander was wounded in the gunfire exchange. President Donald Trump was present at the White House during the incident but was not impacted.

articles.title: Kerala seeks urgent intervention over CBSE Plus Two evaluation complaints - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's General Education Minister N. Samsudheen has requested the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) and the Union government to intervene in the controversy surrounding the evaluation of CBSE Class XII examination papers under the On-Screen Marking (OSM) system.  Samsudheen cited concerns about low marks, unclear answer sheets, and delays in revaluation processes. Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas has accused the Central government of failing to address recurring irregularities in centrally-conducted examinations, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

articles.title: What to know about Cape Verde at World Cup 2026 | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cape Verde, an archipelago of 10 islands in the Atlantic Ocean, is making its World Cup debut in North America.  The team qualified directly after a strong performance in the first round of CAF qualifying, topping a difficult group that included Cameroon and Angola. Bubista, the national team's head coach, has instilled a winning identity in the team, which includes key players like Dailon Livramento, Diney, Jamiro Monteiro, and Willy Semedo.  They will be competing in Group H alongside Spain, Uruguay, and Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Former prosecutor pursued by Trump calls for crackdown on election lies: ‘Lying can be held to account’ | US politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andrew Weissmann, a former federal prosecutor and FBI general counsel, argues for sweeping structural reforms to hold political liars accountable when their lies damage democracy.  He proposes a Truth in Elections Act based on existing law, citing examples like Brazil and the UK where similar measures have been successful. Weissmann believes that while free speech is important, chilling truthful speech is not acceptable. He also criticizes the politicization of prosecutions under the Trump administration, referencing his own experiences with executive orders targeting him and his allies.  Despite facing threats and intimidation, Weissmann remains committed to upholding truth and justice in the US legal system.

articles.title: Ambulance out of CM Revanth’s convoy, now reduced to three from 11 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A. Revanth Reddy, the Chief Minister, has drastically reduced his official convoy from nine vehicles to just three as part of a fuel conservation initiative following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call due to the West Asia crisis.  The decision resulted in the removal of an ambulance equipped with a doctor and support staff, which previously trailed the convoy for emergency medical response. While the reduction has minimized traffic disruptions, it has also raised concerns among security personnel about increased risks associated with commuters deliberately slowing down or filming the convoy.

articles.title: 'Illegal, unacceptable': Pakistan, 13 other nations condemn Somaliland's announcement of opening embassy in Jerusalem - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan, along with 13 other nations, condemned the opening of a purported embassy in occupied Jerusalem by Somaliland. The foreign ministries of these countries expressed their rejection of the "illegal and unacceptable step" as it violates international law and resolutions. They affirmed that East Jerusalem is part of the occupied Palestinian territory and any attempt to alter its status is null and void.  The statement also reiterated support for Somalia's unity, sovereignty, and territorial integrity.

articles.title: The GCC should insure itself against the next Strait of Hormuz crisis | GCC | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The GCC states are facing economic challenges due to the US-Israel-Iran war and its impact on oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz. While some states like Oman have been minimally affected, others such as Kuwait, Bahrain, and Qatar face significant disruptions. The GCC needs to implement collective action to mitigate future threats, including establishing swap arrangements that allow for alternative delivery routes and risk mitigation.  These swaps could involve physical, contractual, or quality exchanges of commodities between member states, potentially requiring coordination among national oil companies, refiners, traders, insurers, banks, and buyers in Asia and Europe. The UAE, Oman, and Saudi Arabia have the potential to play a key role in facilitating these arrangements due to their export capacity, infrastructure, and trading expertise.

articles.title: People trapped under collapsed building in Philippines
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty people are feared trapped under the rubble of a collapsed nine-storey building in Angeles, Philippines, with rescue efforts underway.  24 people have been rescued from the site so far, including two from a nearby hotel struck by falling debris. The cause of the collapse is still being investigated, but officials believe many of those trapped are construction workers who were unable to escape in time.

articles.title: Nationwide pressed to address ‘emerging governance issues’ as AGM looms | Nationwide | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nationwide, under pressure from Navendu Mishra, a Stockport Labour MP, is facing scrutiny over its governance practices.  Mishra has raised concerns about the bundling of voting options and lack of board seats for members, echoing similar issues raised by Rachel Reeves, the chancellor. The MP also criticized the use of "quick vote" options at annual general meetings (AGMs), arguing it reduces scrutiny and favors incumbents. Nationwide maintains that online-only AGMs have increased participation and defends its quick vote system as user-friendly.

articles.title: India voices concern on US visas but sees alignment with Rubio - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India expressed concern over recent US visa restrictions, particularly those targeting Indian tech workers. Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, India's foreign minister, criticized the Trump administration's approach to immigration while acknowledging broad alignment on other issues with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.  Rubio emphasized shared values and strategic partnership between the two countries despite recent policy shifts that have strained relations.

articles.title: Israeli attack on Gaza kills three family members, including infant | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces carried out an air raid on a home in the Nuseirat refugee camp, killing Mohammad Abu Mallouh, his wife Alaa Zaqlan, and their child Osama.  The attack resulted in the deaths of three family members, including a six-month-old child. Medical workers confirmed the casualties, while Israel has yet to issue a statement regarding the incident. The attack occurred despite ongoing ceasefire efforts brokered by the United States, with Hamas and Israel accusing each other of violating the agreement.

articles.title: Bolivian minister's convoy ambushed while overseeing roadblock clearance
articles.rephrased_article: Mauricio Zamora, Bolivia's public works minister, was briefly ambushed while overseeing the clearing of roadblocks by protesters. The incident occurred in Copata on Saturday afternoon when Zamora's vehicle was targeted with stones and dynamite.  Protests have intensified this week, with clashes between demonstrators and security forces in La Paz, as trade unions and supporters of former President Evo Morales demand the resignation of President Rodrigo Paz over his austerity measures and alleged US involvement.

articles.title: With oil markets nearing the danger zone, a US-Iran deal can’t come soon enough | Heather Stewart | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Oil markets are approaching a dangerous tipping point as tensions between the US and Iran have disrupted global supply chains. The International Energy Agency (IEA) warns that oil stocks are being depleted at record rates, with prices remaining below historical highs but poised for significant increases if the strait of Hormuz remains closed.  Several analysts predict a "forced" adjustment to energy demand as prices rise, potentially leading to economic disruption and shortages. The US is facing increased costs for consumers due to rising global energy prices, while the Institute for International Finance (IIF) warns that the ripple effects of the disruption are spreading beyond oil markets, impacting other commodities like LNG and fertilizers.

articles.title: Security forces kill 11 terrorists in KP's North Waziristan: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Security forces in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's North Waziristan district have killed 11 terrorists, identified as members of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (Fitna-al-Khawarij) during a series of intelligence-based operations over the past 48 hours.  Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the slain individuals, who were actively involved in numerous terrorist activities. The ISPR stated that sanitisation operations continue to eliminate remaining terrorists, as Pakistan's counter-terrorism campaign continues with full force to eradicate foreign-sponsored terrorism within the country.

articles.title: Clashes in Belgrade as student-led protests demand elections | Police News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Students and antigovernment protesters clashed with riot police in Belgrade on Saturday, demanding early elections and the rule of law. The demonstrations followed an anti-government rally organized by a youth movement that has challenged President Aleksandar Vucic’s hardline rule for over a year.  The protests were sparked by a train station tragedy in November 2024, which led to calls for accountability and corruption investigations.  Vucic, who was on a state visit to China, criticized the protesters' "violent nature" and vowed that Serbia would continue functioning within the law. The Council of Europe’s commissioner for human rights, Michael O’Flaherty, has expressed concern over the deterioration of Serbia's human rights situation and reported instances of police protecting attackers against journalists and protesters.

articles.title: Iran’s leader and security council ‘still need to approve’ peace deal with US | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump claimed a peace deal with Iran has been largely negotiated, but Iranian officials stated that one or two clauses need clarification before the memorandum of understanding can be sent to Iran's supreme national security council and supreme leader. The proposed deal reportedly offers sanctions relief in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and negotiating on its nuclear program over the next 60 days starting June 5th in Pakistan.  Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian expressed jubilant mood, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the deal aims to address Iran's nuclear ambitions and open the Strait of Hormuz. Republican hawks criticized the proposed agreement as too lenient towards Iran, with former CIA Director Mike Pompeo calling it a "playbook" for building a WMD program.

articles.title: Civilians must not be attacked ‘anywhere’, Pakistan tells UNSC - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's ambassador to the UN, Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, urged an immediate ceasefire and renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war in Ukraine during a UN Security Council emergency meeting.  He emphasized that civilians must not be attacked in armed conflict and called for lasting peace through dialogue and cessation of hostilities. Unicef director of operations and advocacy, Edem Wosornu, stated that nearly 16,000 civilians have been killed and over 44,000 injured in Ukraine since the war began in February 2022, while Ted Chaiban, deputy executive director of Unicef, highlighted that more than 3,400 children have been killed or injured since the escalation of the war in 2022.

articles.title: US, Iran inch closer to deal to end the war: What to know | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that a deal between the United States, Iran, and several other countries in the region has been largely negotiated, with details to be announced soon. The proposed memorandum of understanding (MoU) reportedly includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz, formally ending the US-Israel war on Iran, and opening a 30-day negotiation window for a broader peace agreement. Iran officials have confirmed negotiations are ongoing but pushed back against some of Trump's claims, emphasizing that major disagreements remain, particularly regarding the status of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s nuclear program, and conflicts involving Tehran-backed groups in Lebanon. The main sticking points include the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's nuclear program, and potential reparations for the conflict. While some analysts believe a deal is achievable, others highlight the need for Israel to acquiesce to ensure its success.

articles.title: Former prosecutor calls for EU statute blocking US sanctions on ICC members | International criminal court | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A former ICC prosecutor, Fatou Bensouda, called for an EU-wide statute blocking US sanctions on the court's officials.  She argued that the sanctions are coercive attempts to interfere with the court's judicial functions and represent a misuse of international law. Bensouda criticized the lack of concrete action from states parties, including the Dutch government, which has signed an agreement to protect ICC personnel but has done little in practice to defend the court. She urged for "structural resistance" through legal mechanisms and financial safeguards for the court and its staff.  The US imposed sanctions on 11 ICC officials in response to the court's decision to issue arrest warrants for Israeli cabinet members, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

articles.title: Iran Nuclear Deal: Iran agrees to give up enriched uranium as deal with Donald Trump 'largely negotiated': Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has agreed in principle to give up its stockpile of highly enriched uranium as part of a proposed agreement with the United States, according to The New York Times.  The deal, aimed at ending the ongoing conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, would see Iran relinquish the uranium stockpile through negotiations later.  While President Donald Trump has described the deal as "largely negotiated", Iranian officials have maintained that nuclear issues are not currently part of the immediate discussions. The proposed agreement could include a formal declaration ending the war, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and launching fresh negotiations over Iran’s nuclear program lasting between 30 and 60 days.

articles.title: 25 terrorists killed in Bannu clash - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A fierce clash between police, a peace committee, and terrorists in Bannu district resulted in the deaths of at least 25 terrorists, two police officers, and two civilians.  Police sources confirmed that the operation was launched after receiving information about the presence of a large number of terrorists in the area. The Lakki Marwat police peace committee also arrived to support the Bannu police.  The operation led to the deaths of two key terrorist commanders, Zmari Noor and Abdullah.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Loss of life, including civilians, in a clash with police raises serious concerns.

articles.title: Marco Rubio says ‘significant progress’ made in US-Iran talks to end war | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, United States Secretary of State, stated that significant progress has been made in talks to end the US-Israeli war on Iran, with a potential memorandum of understanding aiming to restore shipping levels through the Strait of Hormuz to pre-war levels within 30 days.  Tasnim News Agency, an Iranian news outlet close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), reported that this agreement would also include the lifting of the US naval blockade on Iranian ports and the release of some frozen Iranian funds. The potential deal, according to Tasnim, would address President Trump's concerns about the Strait of Hormuz and could potentially lead to a world without fear of an Iranian nuclear weapon.

articles.title: What may be included in proposed Iran ceasefire deal? | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has stated that a "memorandum of understanding" in talks to end the US-Israel war on Iran has been largely negotiated. The deal would involve a 60-day ceasefire, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and discussions on limiting Iran's nuclear program.  Iran would agree to clear mines in the strait and lift tolls on ships, while the US would lift its blockade on Iranian ports. However, there is no mention of Iran handing over its highly enriched uranium stockpile or curbing its ballistic missile program.

articles.title: School, residential buildings hit as Russia pounds Ukraine capital Kyiv with missiles, drones; 4 dead - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Russia launched a massive missile and drone attack on Kyiv, Ukraine, early Sunday morning, striking residential areas, a school, and commercial buildings. The attack resulted in at least four deaths and numerous injuries, with fires erupting in multiple districts and forcing residents into underground shelters.  Ukraine's military administration reported damage to several districts across the capital, including a school hit during an ongoing strike drone attack. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned of potential retaliation from Russia following recent Ukrainian attacks in occupied territory.

articles.title: India, U.S. looking at firming up trade deal soon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the upcoming trade agreement between India and the United States will be "beneficial" and "sustainable," addressing national interests for both nations.  Rubio, during a visit to India, emphasized that the agreement is part of a broader effort by the Trump administration to rebalance U.S. trade globally. He highlighted the imbalance in the current trade relationship with India and stated that the US seeks mutually beneficial arrangements with all countries involved. The Secretary of State also noted that the trade delegation from the United States will visit India soon to further discussions on the proposed agreement.

articles.title: Heatstroke kills 16 in southern India as temperatures climb - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: At least 16 people have died of heatstroke in southern India this summer, according to officials, as a severe heatwave grips the country.  The India Meteorological Department predicted above-normal temperatures and intense heatwave conditions earlier this week, with several cities exceeding 45 degrees Celsius. The Telangana government has urged residents to take precautions during heatwaves, particularly vulnerable groups like the elderly, children, and pregnant women.

articles.title: Senegal football fans return home after royal pardon in Morocco | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: King Mohammed VI of Morocco granted a humanitarian pardon to 15 Senegalese football supporters who were jailed following the chaotic Africa Cup of Nations final in January. The supporters, arrested for hooliganism after Senegal's victory over Morocco, returned home on Sunday and were welcomed by Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye.  The incident has strained relations between the two countries but the pardon was granted to mend ties.

articles.title: UK supply chain unprepared for major shocks such as war, report warns | Defence policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The National Preparedness Commission (NPC) has warned that Britain's supply chains are unprepared for major shocks, such as war with Russia. The report highlights the need for more robust stockpiling of critical medicines and food supplies, as well as a shift in government thinking from "why not stockpile" to "how and where."  The NPC also points out the UK's vulnerability due to factors like US nationalism, EU collaborations, China's manufacturing, and Russia's war economy. The report urges bolder action to ensure Britain's resilience against potential future crises.

articles.title: Warren Buffett sits on $400 bn cash as Michael Burry warns of AI bubble. Is a massive market crash coming? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Berkshire Hathaway's record cash hoard of nearly $400 billion is being held back by Buffett, who believes current market conditions are not ideal for aggressive investment.  Analyst Michael Burry remains skeptical about the AI boom, citing indicators similar to the Dotcom crash. Meanwhile, South Korea and Taiwan have emerged as global stock market leaders, overtaking established Western exchanges like the UK and France. The surge in these markets is fueled by investor demand for AI-related stocks, particularly in Taiwan, where TSMC's dominance has contributed significantly to the market capitalization.

articles.title: 'Either we sign a deal or hit them harder': Trump says Iran deal has '50/50' chances - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated that he would meet with advisors to review Iran's latest offer and decide on a final decision regarding military action.  He expressed optimism about securing a "good" agreement, but warned of the possibility of a more aggressive approach.  The diplomatic efforts involve multiple Middle Eastern countries, including Pakistan, which has been mediating between Iran and the United States.  Regional mediators, such as Qatar, Egypt, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan, have been engaged in talks to bridge differences between Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and US negotiators.  The proposed agreement reportedly includes the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, easing of the US blockade on Iran, and the release of frozen Iranian funds.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz showcases agri, IT, SEZs, mines and minerals as key areas for Pak-China cooperation - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif highlighted four key areas for Pakistan-China cooperation during his visit to China, including agriculture, IT, Special Economic Zones (SEZs), and mines and minerals. He emphasized the potential of agricultural trade with China, calling for joint ventures in sectors like textiles and leather. DPM Ishaq Dar, accompanied by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, arrived in Beijing to participate in the 2nd Pakistan-China Political Parties Forum and the 4th CPEC Political Parties Joint Consultation Mechanism.  Dar highlighted the economic revival agenda of the Pakistani government and expressed confidence in the success of joint ventures between Pakistani and Chinese companies.

articles.title: Iran war day 86: Trump announces potential deal amid ‘cloud of mistrust’ | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced progress on an agreement with Iran, potentially reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil chokepoint.  The US president described the memorandum of understanding as a "Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE" and said it would be finalized soon. While Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif of Pakistan, who is mediating the talks, stated that negotiations will happen "very soon," Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed skepticism about the agreement, calling some of Trump's claims inconsistent with reality.  The potential deal has been met with mixed reactions from both sides and remains subject to further discussion.

articles.title: Irish gangland figure fails in Dublin byelection bid for seat in parliament | Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gerry “the monk” Hutch, an Irish gangland figure, failed to secure a parliamentary seat in a Dublin byelection. Daniel Ennis of the Social Democrats won the contest with 12,050 first-preference votes, defeating other candidates including Janice Boylan from Sinn Féin and Janet Horner from the Green party.  The election was held to fill the vacancy left by Paschal Donohoe, who resigned as a finance minister for a World Bank position. The victory of Ennis and the Social Democrats marks a shift towards progressive politics, while Hutch's defeat is seen as a relief for establishment candidates.

articles.title: Cooling appliances’ demand surges ahead of Eidul Azha - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Despite rising living costs, appliance sales have increased in the lead-up to Eidul Azha. Sohail Malik, finance secretary of the Karachi Electronic Dealers Association (KEDA), reported a 25-30% increase in refrigerator and deep freezer sales compared to last year.  Pak Elektron (PAEL), a leading appliance manufacturer, attributes this growth to consumers' need for cooling appliances to store Qurbani meat. The company projects strong recovery in appliance sales due to economic stability, easing import restrictions, lower interest rates, and increased consumer financing.

articles.title: Squeals of horror over price caps – but how are we going to fix our broken food system? | Food & drink industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Treasury is asking UK supermarkets to cap price rises on essential foods in response to rising food prices, a move met with criticism from industry figures. The surge in food prices is attributed to global factors like the Iran war and a record-breaking El Niño event, highlighting vulnerabilities in the global food system.  These disruptions, coupled with climate change impacts like drought and extreme weather events, are causing significant challenges for British farmers and increasing the cost of living crisis.  The UK's reliance on imports for key resources like fertilizer and fossil gas further exacerbates these issues. The government acknowledges the need for a more resilient food system but faces resistance from market-driven approaches.

articles.title: Bomb attack in Pakistan’s Balochistan province kills more than 20 people | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A bomb attack in Quetta, the capital of Pakistan's Balochistan province, killed at least 20 people and injured over 50 others. The Balochistan Liberation Army claimed responsibility for the explosion which occurred when a train passed through the city.  The blast caused several carriages to overturn and catch fire, damaging nearby houses and buildings.  Hospitals in Quetta declared a state of emergency as medical staff were ordered to remain on duty.

articles.title: Cricket fandom is already digital. Fan tokens could be the next mov - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Premier League (IPL) is exploring the use of fan tokens to enhance fan engagement.  Chiliz, a blockchain-based sports platform, has partnered with several European football clubs to launch digital fan tokens that offer exclusive experiences like voting on decisions and access to merchandise. The IPL's large and digitally entrenched fanbase makes it an ideal market for this technology. Fan tokens could provide fans with perks such as early access to tickets, signed merchandise, behind-the-scenes content, loyalty rewards, and meet-and-greets.  However, the success of fan token implementation hinges on ensuring that they remain accessible and fun for fans rather than overly financialized.

articles.title: 'Obsession with our country's most cherished structure': Trump reacts to White House shooting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump reacted to a shooting near the White House, praising Secret Service and law enforcement for their swift action that resulted in the suspect's death. The suspect, identified as Nasire Best, was shot by Secret Service personnel after allegedly firing multiple rounds at officers stationed near a security checkpoint.  The incident occurred while Trump was inside the White House during diplomatic discussions related to Iran and a proposed peace framework involving Middle Eastern nations.

articles.title: 2008 railway exam assault: Raj Thackeray's role in instigating attack not proved, says court - The Hindu
